# E0501: effect name as a row variable

`panic` and `alloc` are inferred, never written in a row. To forbid one, write `without alloc` after the signature.

- Rule: [`effects.effect-names`](../../reference/12-effects.md#effects.effect-names)
- Reported at: the row variable, where it is declared or written.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `items` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0501:1
fn squares(n: i64) -> List<i64> / alloc { [n * n] }
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
fn squares(n: i64) -> List<i64> { [n * n] }
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0501_effect_name_as_a_row_variable.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0501_effect_name_as_a_row_variable.lt):

```text
── EFFECT NAME AS A ROW VARIABLE ── E0501_effect_name_as_a_row_variable.lt:1:35  [E0501]

`alloc` is an implicit effect, which is never written:

  1 │ fn squares(n: i64) -> List<i64> / alloc { [n * n] }
    │                                   ^^^^^

`panic` and `alloc` are inferred, never written in a row. To forbid one, write
`without alloc` after the signature.

To fix it, delete it:

  1 │ fn squares(n: i64) -> List<i64> / alloc { [n * n] }
    │                                --------
```
